activity.title: We built pFOG, a wearable device that helps Parkinson’s patients overcome freezing episodes, and won 1st place at the UC Berkeley AI Hackathon! Freezing of Gait (FOG) is a dangerous symptom of Parkinson’s where patients suddenly lose the ability to walk, often causing falls and serious injury. Recent research shows that mechanical stimulation to the leg can restore movement almost instantly. This weekend, at Cal Hacks my team ( Shuyu van Kerkwijk , Harry Cheng , and Isabel Lew) and I built a device to automate this treatment. Our 1D-CNN + LSTM model detects FOG in real time using IMU data. When a freezing episode is detected, a robotic wearable delivers a targeted "poke" to help the person resume walking. We also built a web interface for easy data collection, labeling, training, and inference so that anyone can personalize it to their unique gait. Medical robotics has the potential to empower millions to live fuller lives, and we hope pFOG is a small but meaningful poke in this direction. devpost: https://lnkd.in/gP68Kb5V research inspiration: https://lnkd.in/gdRNsANV

Did you know that 20,000 whales lose their lives to ship strikes every year? This tragedy is avoidable: in many cases, reducing ship speeds and rerouting to avoid high-risk areas comes at little to no cost to ship operators. At DeltaHacks , we built a solution in under 24 hours. WhaleBeing visualizes ship routes on top of a dynamically predicted whale distribution. To produce the distribution, we implemented a prediction model based on a research paper that uses satellite data of habitat suitability. We then developed our own algorithm to calculate route risk scores by analyzing whale distribution weights near route nodes, offering an actionable insight. We won 1st place overall out of 134 teams and also received the Dyson Innovation Award. Part of our winnings went toward whale conservation efforts, and we aim to scale WhaleBeing with better data/models and route suggestion feature. Ultimately, we hope to propose policy changes using WhaleBeing’s impact evaluation for companies. If you're interested in working with us, feel free to reach out! 🐋 Built with my amazing team Lucas Liao , Gordon Zhang , and Nathan Li. devpost for more details: https://lnkd.in/gmiGqmKn prediction model source: https://lnkd.in/grDk6YcA

Today, we’re announcing Andera 's $37M series A led by Lightspeed with participation from Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) , A*, and Pear VC to build the future of AI auditing. At Andera, we’re building agents to automate the thousands of hours of manual work that our Fortune 10 clients do by hand every day. Our clients have deployed us across SOX, cybersecurity, operational audits and more. Auditors should be empowered to do more with less. As the world has gotten more digitized, auditor’s technology has not kept up. Now, they are left in spots where millions of new transactions could have happened at a company but they only have the time to check a sampling of them by hand. We believe the best product in this space should be built by auditors, for auditors. As such, half of our team are some of the most talented engineers in the Bay, and the other half are the most sharp and gifted auditors we have met. Together, we have solved novel problems in out of distribution data reasoning and have served our fortune 10 clients by turning weeks worth of work into minutes. To our investors, thank you for your unrelenting belief as we continue to transform this industry. To everyone at Andera, thank you for the blood sweat and tears each and every one of you has put into the journey so far while being the most enjoyable group of people I have worked with. And to our customers, thank you for choosing us in a sea of other providers. We’re honored to support you.
